searchText: What time gap are we looking at between mainnet and Goerli? Or will TTDs be set for both at the same time? After Goerli successfully merges, then the TTD for mainnet will be selected. TY Micah! 6 months for withdrawals is the estimate I’ve seen floating around Certainly not the Dec timeline that others have been saying on CT What's CT, and that must be good Hopium they're smoking. I am eternally optimistic. As such I trust my cracked, cloudy crystal ball that foresees merge by mid-October, and withdrawals by March/April. It's quite possible both of those dates are FAR too naive. A slightly more conservative and still optimistic prediction would be merge in 2022, withdrawals in 2023. "Optimistic" as in "there are no fundamental issues with merge design, and it's just a matter of hammering on implementations until we trust them" If that doesn't hold true, all bets are off. While I'm bloviating: If Ethereum merges and promptly stops finalizing because >1/3rd of stake didn't know how to follow instructions on how to set up a merge-ready 1:1 CL:EL setup, and there are no other major issues, I'd consider that a rousing success. Given the amount of money at stake 🥁 , I'd expect misconfigurations to be corrected post-haste and the chain to start finalizing again. Does someone have a website prepped that has a running total of the amount of money lost per minute because people couldn't bother to read the instructions? I'd wager ethereum pools ( https://twitter.com/EthereumPools) could have that up + name everyone who misconfigured😅 Is there a date yet for Goerli testnet merge? Sorry if this is explained elsewhere, I don't really keep up with this discord as much. The Merge is, imo, the single biggest event so far in a stakers crypto life. It's also a huge event in the crypto world. There will be enough news and talk of it that I'm sure no staker will miss. Sepolina was just dev complacency and boredom with doing the same thing for so many forks and shadow forks so far. not yet! Does someone have the blockhash of the sepolia merge block? https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/692062809701482577/995001169917268039 bah i thought that'd be the link to beaconcha.in... but that should be what you want <@508125616940515329> Thanks 🙂 I mean the ETH1 block with the total difficulty of 1700...000 should be able to get the block from execution payload of that eth2 block... but someone might be able to provide the actual you can get hash from beaconcha.in That block from beaconcha.in does not seem to have the right difficulty But, I found it 🙂 https://sepolia.etherscan.io/block/1450408 The next block is the first post-merge block I don't have a beacon client setup and this is weird, my Geth tries to merge on a different block? `INFO [07-11|23:34:41.660] Legacy sync reached merge threshold number=1,450,409 hash=c2414f..d1682f td=17,000,175,511,713,604 ttd=17,000,000,000,000,000` There can be multiple siblings in the network Yes I understand that, but I would not expect this on sepolia 🤔 Your node will reorg once a beacon node is connected Great, thanks 🙂 This also implies that my peer I have connected too is also on the "wrong" chain? The miner produced lots and lots of siblings If you only have one peer than yeah most likely You can and will connect to other peers though I guess this makes sense also the non-merge-ready peers would always reorg if there is a higher TTD block purposefully? or is this a product of the way the noe it's connected to works Especially if miners keep mining to compete for it maybe geth keeps returning a new block for getWork because the old block mined cant be imported I guess what you could do is make a "longer" (higher block num) chain trying to get to merge-TTD minus 1, and then instantly mine (timestamp +1 sec) a block on it to get the highest TTD? A mixture of too much hashrate for too little mining pool and to low difficulty yes that too as in * produces a candidate block * block mined * geth can't import * produces another candidate block with same parent Thats why TTD is based on difficulty not blocknumber, to do this you would need > 51% Yup, great 🙂 Okay very interesting, thanks all! 😄 how robust is prev randao? could someone make a slot machine on it? for example, what i mean is: how unpredictable is it?
